name: St. John Chrysostom
title: Archbishop of Constantinople
bio: Renowned preacher and Archbishop of Constantinople, celebrated for his eloquence and his liturgy still used in the Orthodox Church today.

name: St. George
title: Great Martyr
bio: A Roman soldier martyred for his Christian faith, venerated across the Orthodox world as a symbol of courage and the slayer of the dragon.

name: St. Mary of Egypt
title: Venerable
bio: A former sinner who repented and lived decades alone in the desert beyond the Jordan, becoming a model of repentance and asceticism.

locations.label: Desert of repentance — beyond the Jordan

name: St. Gregory Palamas
title: Archbishop of Thessalonica
bio: A monk of Mount Athos and later Archbishop of Thessalonica, he defended the hesychast practice of contemplative prayer against the rationalist Barlaam of Calabria, teaching that God's uncreated energies can truly be experienced by the faithful.

name: St. Nectarios of Aegina
title: Metropolitan of Pentapolis, Wonderworker
bio: Born Anastasios Cephalas, he served as Metropolitan of Pentapolis before being unjustly removed from his post; he later founded Holy Trinity Monastery on Aegina, where he spent his final years and is remembered for many posthumous healing miracles.

name: St. Spyridon of Trimythous
title: Bishop, Wonderworker
bio: A simple Cypriot shepherd who became Bishop of Trimythous and attended the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea, where he famously explained the Holy Trinity using a piece of brick; his incorrupt relics are now venerated in Corfu, of which he is patron saint.

locations.label: Episcopal see and death — Trimythous, Cyprus

name: St. Dionysios of Zakynthos
title: Archbishop, Venerable
bio: Born Draganigos Sigouros, he became a monk and later Archbishop of Aegina before retiring to a monastery on his native Zakynthos; he is remembered above all for forgiving the man who, unknowingly, had killed his own brother.

locations.label: Birthplace, monastic life, and relics — Zakynthos

name: St. Cosmas of Aetolia
title: Hieromartyr, Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: A monk of Mount Athos who spent 25 years traveling on foot throughout Greece and Albania, founding over 200 schools and preaching to villagers left without churches or priests after centuries of Ottoman rule, before being martyred on charges brought against him.

name: St. Basil the Great
title: Archbishop of Caesarea, one of the Three Holy Hierarchs
bio: Bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia and a leading 4th-century theologian, he defended Orthodoxy against Arianism and founded the Basiliad, a combined poorhouse, hospital, and hostel for the destitute outside his city.

locations.label: Birthplace, episcopal see, and death — Caesarea, Cappadocia

name: St. Gregory the Theologian
title: Archbishop of Constantinople, one of the Three Holy Hierarchs
bio: A close friend of St. Basil the Great, he was chosen Archbishop of Constantinople by the Second Ecumenical Council for his defense of the Trinity against Arianism, before retiring to Nazianzus for the rest of his life.

name: St. Catherine of Alexandria
title: Great Martyr
bio: A learned and noble young woman of Alexandria who confounded fifty pagan philosophers sent to refute her Christian faith and was martyred under Emperor Maximinus; her relics were later found at the monastery bearing her name on Mount Sinai.

name: St. Panteleimon
title: Great Martyr, Unmercenary Healer
bio: A physician of Nicomedia who treated the poor and sick without charge in the name of Christ, he was martyred under Emperor Maximian after healing a paralyzed man before the emperor's own eyes; he is invoked among the unmercenary healer-saints.

name: St. Anthony the Great
title: Venerable, Father of Monasticism
bio: Born to a wealthy family in Egypt, he sold his possessions to follow Christ's call to the poor and withdrew into the desert, becoming the leader of the Desert Fathers and the model for all later Christian monasticism.

locations.label: Monastery and relics — Eastern Desert, Egypt

name: St. Sabbas the Sanctified
title: Venerable
bio: A Cappadocian monastic who settled in the Judean desert and founded the Great Lavra (Mar Saba), composing the Jerusalem Typikon that shaped monastic and liturgical practice across the Orthodox world.

locations.label: Monastery and relics — Mar Saba, Judean Desert

name: St. Demetrius of Thessaloniki
title: Great Martyr, Myrrh-streamer
bio: A high-ranking Christian official martyred under Emperor Galerius, he is venerated as the patron and protector of Thessaloniki, where a miraculous flow of fragrant myrrh was later found at his tomb.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom and relics — Thessaloniki

name: St. Paisios of Mount Athos
title: Venerable, Elder
bio: Born Arsenios Eznepidis, his family fled Asia Minor for Greece in his infancy; he became a monk of Mount Athos known for his gentle counsel to the thousands of pilgrims who sought him out, and was canonized in 2015.

locations.label: Death and relics — Souroti, near Thessaloniki

name: St. Gerasimos of Kephalonia
title: Venerable, Wonderworker
bio: Born to a noble Byzantine family, he lived as a hermit on Mount Athos, in Jerusalem, Sinai, Egypt, Crete, and Zakynthos before settling in a cave in Kephalonia, where he restored a church and founded a convent; he is now the island's patron saint.

name: St. Nicholas of Myra
title: Archbishop of Myra, Wonderworker
bio: Bishop of Myra in Lycia and participant in the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea, he is venerated throughout the world for his generosity to the poor and his protection of sailors, children, and the falsely accused. His relics were translated to Bari, Italy in 1087.

locations.label: Episcopal see and death — Myra (Demre), Lycia

name: St. John the Baptist
title: Prophet, Forerunner, Baptist
bio: The last of the Old Testament prophets and Forerunner of Christ, he proclaimed repentance in the Judean desert, baptized Jesus in the Jordan, and was martyred by Herod Antipas at the request of Salome. He holds the unique liturgical title “Greater than the prophets.”

locations.label: Baptism of Christ — Qasr al-Yahud, Jordan River

name: St. Athanasios the Great
title: Archbishop of Alexandria
bio: Archbishop of Alexandria who championed Nicene orthodoxy against Arianism throughout his life, enduring five exiles at the hands of Arian emperors. His phrase “Athanasios contra mundum” captures his solitary defense of the full divinity of Christ.

locations.label: Birthplace, episcopal see, and relics — Alexandria

name: St. Cyril of Alexandria
title: Archbishop of Alexandria
bio: Archbishop of Alexandria who presided over the Third Ecumenical Council of Ephesus (431 AD), which confirmed the title Theotokos (“God-bearer”) for the Virgin Mary against the teaching of Nestorius. His prolific theological writings earned him the title “Seal of the Fathers.”

name: St. Makarios of Egypt
title: Venerable, Desert Father
bio: A disciple of St. Anthony the Great who settled in the Scetis desert of Egypt and became one of the most celebrated Desert Fathers, attracting thousands of monks to the Wadi Natrun. He is the reputed author of the Fifty Spiritual Homilies on the life of inner prayer.

locations.label: Monastic life and relics — Wadi el-Natrun (Scetis)

name: St. Seraphim of Sarov
title: Venerable, Wonderworker
bio: A monk of Sarov in Russia who spent years in hermitage and later opened his cell to thousands of pilgrims, greeting each with the words “My joy!” He taught that the aim of the Christian life is the acquisition of the Holy Spirit, and remains one of the most beloved saints of the Russian Church.

locations.label: Monastic life and death — Sarov, Russia

name: St. Porphyrios of Kafsokalyvia
title: Venerable, Elder
bio: A Greek elder who spent decades as a confessor near Athens, renowned for his gift of clairvoyance and his joyful, Christ-centred spiritual direction. He was canonized in 2013 and his collected conversations have been read by millions across the Orthodox world.

locations.label: Priestly ministry and death — Milesi, near Athens

name: St. Abercius of Hierapolis
title: Bishop, Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: Bishop of Hierapolis in Phrygia in the late 2nd century, renowned as a missionary and wonder-worker. His famous epitaph, discovered in 1882, is one of the oldest Christian inscriptions and describes his travels to Rome and Mesopotamia proclaiming the faith.

locations.label: Episcopal see and death — Hierapolis (Pamukkale), Phrygia

name: St. Agafia (Agatha) of Rome
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A young noblewoman of Sicily martyred under Emperor Decius around 250 AD for refusing to renounce her Christian faith and her vow of virginity. She is venerated as the patron saint of Catania and of Sicily, and is invoked against fire and breast diseases.

name: St. Alexander of Alexandria
title: Archbishop of Alexandria
bio: Archbishop of Alexandria who convened the local synod that first condemned Arianism, then led the Orthodox delegation to the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea in 325 AD alongside his deacon Athanasios. He is venerated for his defense of the full divinity of Christ before it was formally defined.

name: St. Alexios, Man of God
title: Venerable
bio: Born to a noble Roman family, Alexios fled his arranged marriage on his wedding night, lived as a beggar in Edessa for seventeen years, then returned to Rome and lived unknown under the staircase of his own family's house until his death. He is a celebrated model of radical humility and voluntary poverty.

locations.label: Seventeen years as a beggar — Edessa (Sanlıurfa)

name: St. Ambrose of Milan
title: Bishop of Milan
bio: Governor of Milan unexpectedly acclaimed as its bishop by the people in 374 AD while still a catechumen. He became one of the great Latin Fathers, championed orthodoxy against Arianism, penned celebrated hymns still sung today, and boldly confronted the Emperor Theodosius over the Massacre of Thessalonica.

name: St. Anastasia the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr, Deliverer from Potions
bio: A Roman noblewoman who used her wealth to minister to Christians imprisoned under Emperor Diocletian, traveling from prison to prison to care for confessors. She was martyred in Sirmium around 304 AD and is venerated across the Orthodox world with the epithet “Deliverer from Potions” for her healing intercessions.

name: Sts. Andronikos and Athanasia
title: Venerable
bio: A married couple of Antioch who, after the death of their two children, mutually agreed to live in consecrated celibacy. Andronikos became a monk in Egypt; Athanasia, unknown to him, also became a monk disguised as a man. They met again years later, and Andronikos only discovered her identity after her death.

name: St. Antipa of Pergamon
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Bishop of Pergamon in Asia Minor, mentioned in the Book of Revelation (2:13) as “my faithful witness who was killed among you.” He was martyred under Emperor Domitian, traditionally by being cast into a red-hot bronze bull used for pagan sacrifices. He is invoked for toothaches.

name: St. Apollinaris of Ravenna
title: Hieromartyr, Bishop
bio: Traditionally a disciple of St. Peter the Apostle, he became the first bishop of Ravenna and was martyred after several exiles for refusing to offer sacrifice to pagan gods. The magnificent Byzantine basilicas of Sant’Apollinare in Classe and Sant’Apollinare Nuovo in Ravenna are dedicated to him.

name: Sts. Aquila and Priscilla
title: Apostles
bio: Jewish Christian tentmakers mentioned repeatedly in the New Testament as close companions of St. Paul the Apostle, who worked alongside him in Corinth and Ephesus. They hosted a church in their home and personally instructed the eloquent Apollos in the Christian faith.

name: St. Arsenios the Great
title: Venerable, Desert Father
bio: A highly educated Roman deacon who served as tutor to the imperial princes Arcadius and Honorius in Constantinople, then at the age of forty renounced everything and became a monk in the Egyptian desert. He is remembered for his maxim: “I have often repented of having spoken, but never of having been silent.”

name: St. Athanasios of Athos
title: Venerable
bio: Founder of the Great Lavra, the oldest and most prestigious monastery on Mount Athos, established in 963 AD with the patronage of Emperor Nikephoros Phokas. He organized cenobitic monastic life on the Holy Mountain and shaped Athonite monasticism for centuries to come.

locations.label: Foundation of the Great Lavra — Mount Athos

name: St. Barbara the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: Daughter of a wealthy pagan of Nicomedia who was locked in a tower by her father to keep her from suitors, she secretly embraced Christianity and had a third window added to her bathhouse in honor of the Trinity. She was tortured and beheaded by her own father after refusing to renounce her faith.

name: St. Blaise of Sebaste
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Sebaste in Armenia and a physician who was said to heal both people and wild animals, he withdrew to a cave during a persecution where he continued his healing ministry. He was arrested, tortured with iron combs, and beheaded, and is invoked to this day against ailments of the throat.

name: St. Boniface of Tarsus
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman servant of dissolute life who was sent by his mistress Aglaida to collect the relics of martyrs in the East, he was so moved by witnessing their courage under torture in Tarsus that he confessed Christ himself and was executed. His own relics were then brought back to Rome by the astonished servants who had accompanied him.

name: St. Charalambos
title: Hieromartyr
bio: An elderly bishop of Magnesia who, at over a hundred years old, was seized during the persecutions of Septimius Severus for continuing to preach Christ. He endured his flesh being flayed with iron hooks without complaint, converting the very soldiers and governor sent to torment him.

name: St. Christina the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: A young woman of Tyre who smashed her father's golden idols and distributed the metal to the poor, she was subjected by him and later by Roman governors to a horrific series of tortures, including being thrown into the sea, all of which she miraculously survived before her eventual martyrdom.

name: St. Clement of Rome
title: Hieromartyr, Pope of Rome
bio: A disciple of the Apostles Peter and Paul who became the fourth Bishop of Rome, he authored an epistle to the Corinthians that is among the earliest surviving Christian writings outside the New Testament. Exiled to Crimea for his preaching, he was drowned in the Black Sea with an anchor tied to his neck.

name: Sts. Cyprian and Justina
title: Hieromartyrs
bio: A renowned pagan sorcerer of Antioch hired to ensnare the Christian maiden Justina, Cyprian found his magic powerless against her prayers and, astonished, converted and burned his books of spells before becoming a bishop. He and Justina were later arrested together and beheaded under Diocletian.

name: St. Daniel the Stylite
title: Venerable
bio: Inspired by St. Symeon the Stylite whom he visited as a young monk, Daniel took up the ascetic discipline of pillar-standing near Constantinople, enduring decades of exposure to the elements. Emperors and patriarchs sought his counsel, and he was even ordained a priest atop his own pillar.

name: St. David of Thessaloniki
title: Venerable
bio: A monk who lived for years in the branches of an almond tree outside Thessaloniki as an extreme act of asceticism, praying exposed to sun and frost. He later left his tree to intercede successfully with the Emperor in Constantinople on behalf of his city, before returning to his monastery to die in peace.

name: St. Dionysius the Areopagite
title: Hieromartyr
bio: A judge of the Areopagus court in Athens who was converted by hearing the Apostle Paul's sermon on the “Unknown God”, he became the first bishop of Athens. Tradition holds he later traveled west to preach the Gospel and was martyred in Lutetia (Paris).

name: St. Ephraim the Syrian
title: Venerable
bio: A deacon and prolific hymnographer of Nisibis and later Edessa, he composed hundreds of hymns and homilies in Syriac defending Orthodox teaching against heresy, many of which remain in liturgical use. His Lenten prayer, “O Lord and Master of my life,” is recited throughout Great Lent in Orthodox churches.

name: St. Eugenia of Rome
title: Martyr
bio: Daughter of a Roman prefect of Egypt, she disguised herself as a man to enter a monastery near Alexandria, eventually being chosen as its abbot without her true identity being known. She was later falsely accused, revealed her identity to clear herself, and was ultimately martyred in Rome under Valerian.

name: St. Eustathios Placidas
title: Great Martyr
bio: A Roman general known as Placidas who converted to Christianity after seeing a vision of Christ between the antlers of a stag while hunting, taking the name Eustathios at baptism. After enduring the loss of his family and fortune as trials of faith, he was ultimately martyred with his wife and sons by being roasted alive in a bronze bull.

name: St. Euthymios the Great
title: Venerable
bio: Born in Melitene in Armenia, he journeyed to the Judean Desert and founded a renowned lavra that became a center of monastic and doctrinal formation, playing a key role in defending Orthodoxy at the Council of Chalcedon. He is honored as one of the great founders of Palestinian monasticism.

locations.label: Foundation of his Lavra — Judean Desert

name: St. Fanourios the Newly-Revealed
title: Great Martyr
bio: Known only from an icon discovered amid the ruins of an ancient church during the excavation of the city walls of Rhodes, depicting scenes of his martyrdom alongside his name, with no other historical record surviving. Devotion to him spread quickly, and to this day the faithful bake “fanouropita” cakes in his honor when seeking help to find lost things.

name: St. Ignatius of Antioch
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Antioch and disciple of the Apostles, thrown to wild beasts in Rome, whose letters to the early Church remain foundational Christian writings.

name: St. Polycarp of Smyrna
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Smyrna and disciple of the Apostle John, burned at the stake for refusing to renounce Christ in old age.

name: St. Irenaeus of Lyons
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Lyons and student of Polycarp, whose writings against heresies shaped early Christian theology.

name: St. Cyprian of Carthage
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Carthage martyred under Emperor Valerian, celebrated for his writings on Church unity.

name: St. Justin the Philosopher
title: Martyr
bio: A pagan philosopher converted to Christianity who defended the faith in his writings before being martyred in Rome.

name: St. Lawrence of Rome
title: Archdeacon and Martyr
bio: A deacon of Rome martyred on a gridiron for distributing the Church's wealth to the poor rather than surrendering it to the state.

name: St. Sebastian
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman soldier martyred for aiding imprisoned Christians, shot with arrows and later clubbed to death.

name: St. Agnes of Rome
title: Virgin Martyr
bio: A young Roman girl martyred for her consecrated virginity, venerated as a model of purity and courage.

name: St. Cecilia
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman noblewoman martyred for her faith, traditionally venerated as patroness of church music.

name: St. Valentine
title: Martyr
bio: A priest of Rome martyred under Claudius II for secretly marrying Christian couples and aiding persecuted believers.

name: St. Pachomius the Great
title: Venerable
bio: An Egyptian monk who founded the first cenobitic monastery, organizing communal monastic life along the Nile.

name: St. Paul of Thebes
title: Venerable
bio: Regarded as the first Christian hermit, who lived nearly a century alone in the Egyptian desert.

name: St. Hilarion the Great
title: Venerable
bio: A disciple of Anthony the Great who brought monasticism from Egypt to Palestine.

locations.label: Discipleship under Anthony the Great — Eastern Desert, Egypt

name: St. John Climacus
title: Venerable
bio: Abbot of Sinai and author of 'The Ladder of Divine Ascent,' a foundational text of Orthodox spirituality.

name: St. Gregory of Sinai
title: Venerable
bio: A monk who revived the practice of hesychasm and spread it among monasteries in Greece and the Balkans.

name: St. Symeon the New Theologian
title: Venerable
bio: A Byzantine monk and mystic whose writings on the vision of divine light influenced Orthodox spirituality.

name: St. Maximus the Confessor
title: Confessor
bio: A monk and theologian who had his tongue and right hand cut off for defending Orthodox Christology, yet never wavered.

name: St. Theodore the Studite
title: Venerable Confessor
bio: Abbot of the Stoudios Monastery who defended the veneration of icons against iconoclast emperors.

name: St. John of Damascus
title: Venerable
bio: A monk and hymnographer of Mar Saba whose writings defended icons and systematized Orthodox theology.

name: St. Sophia and her Daughters Faith, Hope and Love
title: Martyrs
bio: A widow martyred in Rome alongside her three young daughters, Faith, Hope, and Love, for refusing to worship idols.

name: St. Marina the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: A young woman of Antioch in Pisidia tortured and beheaded for her faith, widely venerated across the Orthodox world.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — Antioch of Pisidia

name: St. Euphemia the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: A martyr of Chalcedon whose tomb miraculously confirmed the Orthodox faith at the Fourth Ecumenical Council.

name: St. Paraskevi of Rome
title: Martyr
bio: A Roman virgin martyred for her faith, widely venerated as a healer, especially of eye ailments.

name: St. Kyriaki the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: A young woman of Nicomedia tortured extensively but preserved by God before dying peacefully in prayer.

name: St. Irene the Great Martyr
title: Great Martyr
bio: A young woman converted by St. Timothy and martyred for destroying her family's idols and preaching Christ.

name: St. Menas of Egypt
title: Great Martyr
bio: An Egyptian soldier martyred for confessing Christ, whose shrine near Alexandria became a major pilgrimage site.

name: St. Theodore the Tyro
title: Great Martyr
bio: A young Roman soldier burned to death for setting fire to a pagan temple, remembered for the miracle of kolyva.

name: St. Theodore Stratelates
title: Great Martyr
bio: A military commander of Heraclea Pontica beheaded for his faith after destroying an idol of Artemis.

name: St. Artemios of Antioch
title: Great Martyr
bio: A Roman general martyred under Emperor Julian the Apostate for protesting the persecution of Christians.

name: St. Mercurius of Caesarea
title: Great Martyr
bio: A Roman soldier martyred for his faith, later venerated for miraculously striking down Julian the Apostate.

name: St. Eustratius of Sebaste
title: Martyr
bio: One of the Five Martyrs of Sebaste, a military officer burned alive for his unwavering confession of Christ.

name: The Forty Martyrs of Sebaste
title: Martyrs
bio: Forty Roman soldiers who froze to death on a lake for refusing to renounce Christianity, encouraging one another to the end.

name: St. Acacius of Sinai
title: Venerable
bio: A monk celebrated by St. John Climacus for his perfect obedience even after death.

name: St. Mary Magdalene
title: Myrrhbearer and Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: A devoted follower of Christ, first witness of His Resurrection, later a missionary who reposed in Ephesus.

name: St. Lazarus of the Four Days
title: Righteous
bio: Friend of Christ raised from the dead after four days, who later served as bishop of Kition in Cyprus.

name: St. Joseph of Arimathea
title: Righteous
bio: A secret disciple of Christ who donated his own tomb for the Lord's burial after the Crucifixion.

locations.label: Donated tomb for Christ's burial — Jerusalem

name: St. Nicodemus
title: Righteous
bio: A Pharisee who visited Christ by night and later helped prepare His body for burial.

name: Apostle Thomas
title: Apostle
bio: One of the Twelve Apostles, who doubted the Resurrection until he touched Christ's wounds, later evangelized India.

name: Apostle Bartholomew
title: Apostle
bio: One of the Twelve Apostles who preached in Armenia, where he was martyred by flaying.

name: Apostle Philip
title: Apostle
bio: One of the Twelve Apostles who brought Nathanael to Christ and was later martyred in Hierapolis.

name: Apostle and Evangelist Matthew
title: Apostle and Evangelist
bio: A former tax collector called by Christ to be an Apostle, author of the first Gospel.

name: Apostle James, Son of Zebedee
title: Apostle
bio: Brother of John the Theologian and one of the Twelve, the first Apostle to be martyred, beheaded in Jerusalem.

name: Apostle Andrew the First-Called
title: Apostle
bio: Brother of Peter and the first disciple called by Christ, later crucified on an X-shaped cross in Patras.

name: Apostle Peter
title: Chief Apostle
bio: A fisherman called by Christ who became the foremost of the Apostles, martyred by crucifixion upside down in Rome.

name: Apostle Paul
title: Chief Apostle
bio: Former persecutor of Christians converted on the road to Damascus, becoming the great Apostle to the Gentiles.

name: Apostle and Evangelist Luke
title: Apostle and Evangelist
bio: A physician and companion of Paul who wrote the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles.

name: Apostle and Evangelist Mark
title: Apostle and Evangelist
bio: Author of the Gospel of Mark and founder of the Church of Alexandria, martyred by being dragged through the streets.

name: St. Stephen the Protomartyr
title: Archdeacon and Protomartyr
bio: The first of the seven deacons and the first Christian martyr, stoned to death in Jerusalem.

name: St. Cornelius the Centurion
title: Righteous
bio: A Roman centurion in Caesarea who became the first Gentile convert baptized by the Apostle Peter.

name: St. Helen, Equal-to-the-Apostles
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: Mother of Emperor Constantine who discovered the True Cross in Jerusalem and built many churches.

name: St. Constantine the Great
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: The first Christian Roman Emperor, who legalized Christianity and founded Constantinople as the new capital.

name: St. Vladimir, Equal-to-the-Apostles
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: Grand Prince of Kiev who converted from paganism and brought Christianity to the Rus' people.

name: St. Olga, Equal-to-the-Apostles
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: Grandmother of St. Vladimir and the first ruler of Rus' to embrace Christianity, laying the groundwork for its spread.

name: Sts. Cyril and Methodius
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: Brothers from Thessaloniki who created the Slavic alphabet and translated Scripture, evangelizing the Slavic peoples.

name: St. Patrick of Ireland
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: A Romano-British missionary who brought Christianity to Ireland after years of captivity there as a youth.

name: St. Sergius of Radonezh
title: Venerable
bio: Founder of the Holy Trinity Monastery near Moscow, one of the most beloved monastic saints of Russia.

name: St. Seraphim of Vyritsa
title: Venerable
bio: A successful merchant who became a monk and elder, known for prayer and prophecy during Soviet persecution.

name: St. Xenia of St. Petersburg
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A widow who gave away all her possessions and lived as a homeless fool-for-Christ, beloved for her clairvoyance and charity.

name: St. John of Kronstadt
title: Righteous
bio: A married parish priest renowned for his fervent liturgical life, healings, and care for the poor of Kronstadt.

name: St. Tikhon of Moscow
title: Patriarch and Confessor
bio: Patriarch of Moscow during the Bolshevik Revolution, who steadfastly guided the Church through severe persecution.

name: St. Nikolai Velimirović
title: Bishop
bio: Serbian bishop, theologian, and prisoner at Dachau, celebrated for his writings and pastoral zeal.

name: St. Sava of Serbia
title: Archbishop
bio: First Archbishop of the autocephalous Serbian Church and founder of Hilandar Monastery on Mount Athos.

name: St. Simeon the Myrrh-streaming
title: Venerable
bio: Founder of the Serbian medieval state who became a monk in old age, his relics later streamed myrrh.

name: St. John of Rila
title: Venerable
bio: Bulgaria's patron saint, a hermit whose cave and later monastery became the spiritual heart of Bulgarian monasticism.

name: St. Joasaph of Belgorod
title: Bishop
bio: An 18th-century Russian bishop renowned for his ascetic life, care for the poor, and incorrupt relics.

name: St. Innocent of Alaska
title: Enlightener of the Aleuts and Apostle to America
bio: A missionary priest and later Metropolitan of Moscow who evangelized Alaska and the peoples of the Russian Far East.

name: St. Herman of Alaska
title: Venerable
bio: A Russian monk missionary to Alaska who defended the native Aleut people and lived in ascetic simplicity on Spruce Island.

name: St. Raphael of Brooklyn
title: Bishop
bio: The first Orthodox bishop consecrated in North America, serving Arab Orthodox immigrants across the continent.

name: St. Alexis Toth
title: Confessor
bio: A priest who led the return of many Carpatho-Rusyn parishes in America to Orthodoxy, called the 'Father of the Orthodox Church in America.'

name: St. Luke of Crimea (Voino-Yasenetsky)
title: Bishop and Confessor
bio: A surgeon and archbishop who continued practicing medicine and healing the sick even through Soviet imprisonment and exile.

name: St. Matrona of Moscow
title: Righteous
bio: A blind and paralyzed woman renowned for her prophetic gifts and healings during some of Russia's darkest years.

name: St. Anthony of the Kiev Caves
title: Venerable
bio: Founder of the Kiev Caves Lavra, bringing the monastic tradition of Mount Athos to the Rus' lands.

name: St. Theodosius of the Kiev Caves
title: Venerable
bio: Co-founder of the Kiev Caves Lavra known for his humility, hospitality, and organization of communal monastic life.

name: St. Gregory of Nyssa
title: Hierarch
bio: Bishop of Nyssa and one of the Cappadocian Fathers, celebrated for his mystical theology and defense of Nicene doctrine.

name: St. Epiphanius of Cyprus
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Salamis in Cyprus, a staunch defender of Orthodoxy against heresies of his time.

name: St. Nicholas Planas
title: Righteous
bio: A humble Athenian parish priest of the 19th–20th century renowned for his tireless liturgical devotion and simplicity.

name: St. Arsenios of Paros
title: Venerable
bio: A monk and spiritual father on the island of Paros known for his gift of foresight and healing.

name: St. Savvas the New of Kalymnos
title: Venerable
bio: A monk of Kalymnos in the 19th century known for his extreme asceticism and care for the sick.

name: Sts. Raphael, Nicholas and Irene of Lesvos
title: New Martyrs
bio: A priest, a layman, and a young girl martyred by Ottoman raiders on Lesvos, whose relics were revealed in the 20th century.

name: St. Ephraim of Nea Makri
title: New Martyr
bio: A monk martyred by Ottoman forces in the 15th century, whose relics were revealed near Athens in the 20th century.

name: St. George the New of Ioannina
title: New Martyr
bio: A young Christian craftsman martyred in Ottoman-ruled Ioannina after refusing to convert to Islam.

name: St. Nikodemos the Hagiorite
title: Venerable
bio: A monk of Mount Athos and prolific author who compiled the Philokalia, shaping modern Orthodox spirituality.

name: St. Silouan the Athonite
title: Venerable
bio: A Russian monk of Mount Athos known for his profound humility and the teaching 'keep your mind in hell and despair not.'

name: St. Joseph the Hesychast
title: Venerable
bio: A 20th-century Athonite elder whose disciples revitalized many monasteries of Mount Athos.

name: St. Amphilochios of Patmos
title: Venerable
bio: Abbot of the Monastery of St. John on Patmos, known for his love of nature and gift of spiritual counsel.

name: St. Iakovos (Jacob) Tsalikis
title: Venerable
bio: Abbot of Saint David Monastery in Euboea, revered in modern Greece for his humility and visions of saints.

name: St. Dionysios of Olympus
title: Venerable
bio: A hermit and founder of a monastery on Mount Olympus, celebrated for his austere life of prayer.

name: St. Gerasimos of the Jordan
title: Venerable
bio: A 5th-century abbot near the Jordan River famed for taming a lion that became his devoted companion.

name: St. Onuphrius the Great
title: Venerable
bio: A hermit who spent seventy years alone in the Egyptian desert in extreme asceticism and prayer.

name: Sts. Martha and Mary of Bethany
title: Righteous
bio: Sisters of Lazarus who hosted Christ in their home in Bethany, models of hospitality and devotion.

name: St. Bernice (Veronica)
title: Righteous
bio: Venerated in tradition as the woman healed of a hemorrhage by touching Christ's garment.

name: The Holy Myrrhbearing Women
title: Myrrhbearers
bio: The women disciples who came to anoint Christ's body and were the first to learn of His Resurrection.

name: St. Hermione of Ephesus
title: Martyr
bio: Daughter of the Apostle Philip who had the gift of healing and was martyred under Emperor Trajan.

name: Sts. Zenobius and Zenobia
title: Martyrs
bio: A physician bishop and his sister martyred together in Cilicia under Diocletian's persecution.

name: Sts. Cyrus and John the Unmercenaries
title: Unmercenary Healers
bio: A physician and a soldier who healed the sick without payment and were martyred together in Egypt.

name: Sts. Cosmas and Damian the Unmercenaries
title: Unmercenary Healers
bio: Twin brothers and physicians in Asia Minor who healed the sick free of charge before their martyrdom.

name: St. Hermolaus of Nicomedia
title: Priest-Martyr
bio: A priest who instructed St. Panteleimon in the faith and was martyred alongside two companions in Nicomedia.

name: St. Tryphon of Campsada
title: Martyr
bio: A young goose-herder martyred under Emperor Decius, later venerated as protector of crops and vineyards.

name: Sts. Porphyrios, Baptus and Companions
title: Martyrs
bio: Roman soldiers converted and martyred alongside St. Charalambos after witnessing his miraculous endurance.

name: St. Thecla the Protomartyr
title: Protomartyr Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: A young woman of Iconium converted by hearing St. Paul preach, surviving multiple attempted martyrdoms.

name: St. Pelagia of Antioch
title: Venerable
bio: A repentant actress of Antioch who became a hermit on the Mount of Olives disguised as a monk.

name: St. Mary the Younger
title: Righteous
bio: A pious laywoman of Byzantine Bizye who endured suffering with patience and was glorified after her death.

name: St. Febronia of Nisibis
title: Martyr
bio: A young nun of Nisibis tortured extensively and martyred for refusing marriage and renouncing Christ.

name: St. Drosis of Antioch
title: Martyr
bio: Daughter of Emperor Trajan who secretly buried martyrs and was burned alive when her faith was discovered.

name: St. Domnica of Constantinople
title: Venerable
bio: A founder of a women's monastery in Constantinople renowned for her ascetic virtue and gift of prophecy.

name: St. Theodora of Alexandria
title: Venerable
bio: A repentant woman who lived disguised as a monk in the desert for years to atone for her sins.

name: St. Synkletike of Alexandria
title: Venerable
bio: A desert mother whose sayings on ascetic discipline were preserved among the Apophthegmata Patrum.

name: St. Melania the Younger
title: Venerable
bio: A wealthy Roman noblewoman who renounced her fortune to found monasteries in Jerusalem and North Africa.

name: St. Pulcheria the Empress
title: Righteous
bio: A Byzantine empress who governed with piety and convened the Fourth Ecumenical Council against heresy.

name: St. Theodora the Empress
title: Righteous
bio: A Byzantine empress who restored the veneration of icons, ending the second period of iconoclasm.

name: St. Theophano the Empress
title: Righteous
bio: A pious Byzantine empress known for her charity to the poor and devotion to prayer despite palace intrigue.

name: St. Photios the Great
title: Patriarch
bio: Patriarch of Constantinople and renowned scholar who sent missionaries Cyril and Methodius to the Slavs.

name: St. Tarasios of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: Patriarch who presided over the Seventh Ecumenical Council, restoring the veneration of holy icons.

name: St. Germanus of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: Patriarch deposed for opposing iconoclasm, whose hymns are still sung in Orthodox services today.

name: St. Mark of Ephesus
title: Bishop and Confessor
bio: The sole bishop who refused to sign the Council of Florence's union with Rome, defending Orthodoxy alone.

name: St. Gennadius Scholarios
title: Patriarch
bio: The first Ecumenical Patriarch under Ottoman rule after the fall of Constantinople, guiding the Church through crisis.

name: St. Niphon of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: A Wallachian monk who twice served as Patriarch of Constantinople, known for his humility and reforms.

name: St. Cyprian of Kiev and Moscow
title: Metropolitan
bio: A Bulgarian-born metropolitan who unified the Russian Church and translated important liturgical texts into Slavonic.

name: St. Alexis of Moscow
title: Metropolitan
bio: Metropolitan of Moscow who served as regent for the young Prince Dmitri Donskoi and healed the Tatar khan's mother.

name: St. Peter of Moscow
title: Metropolitan
bio: The first Metropolitan to move his see to Moscow, helping establish the city as the spiritual center of Russia.

name: St. Jonah of Moscow
title: Metropolitan
bio: The first Metropolitan of Moscow elected independently of Constantinople, establishing the autocephaly of the Russian Church.

name: St. Stephen of Perm
title: Bishop
bio: Missionary bishop who created an alphabet for the Zyrian people and translated Scripture into their language.

name: St. Basil the Blessed, Fool-for-Christ
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A Moscow holy fool who fearlessly rebuked Ivan the Terrible, giving his name to the famous cathedral on Red Square.

name: St. Andrew the Fool-for-Christ
title: Fool-for-Christ
bio: A Constantinopolitan slave who feigned madness for Christ's sake and witnessed the vision of the Theotokos's veil.

name: St. Nicholas Cabasilas
title: Righteous
bio: A Byzantine theologian and layman of Thessaloniki celebrated for his writings on the Divine Liturgy and life in Christ.

name: St. Gregory of Narek
title: Venerable and Doctor
bio: An Armenian monk, poet, and theologian, celebrated for his 'Book of Lamentations' and profound spiritual depth.

name: St. Isaac the Syrian
title: Venerable
bio: A bishop who resigned to live as a hermit, whose ascetic homilies remain treasured across Christian traditions.

name: St. James of Nisibis
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Nisibis and participant in the First Ecumenical Council, defender of the city against Persian siege through prayer.

name: St. Babylas of Antioch
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Antioch who barred an emperor from entering the church for shedding innocent blood and was martyred.

name: St. Meletios of Antioch
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop of Antioch who presided at the opening of the Second Ecumenical Council in Constantinople.

name: St. Proclus of Constantinople
title: Patriarch
bio: Patriarch of Constantinople and disciple of St. John Chrysostom, celebrated preacher on the Theotokos.

name: St. Flavian of Constantinople
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Patriarch who was beaten and exiled at the 'Robber Council' of Ephesus for upholding Orthodox Christology.

name: St. Ambrose of Optina
title: Venerable
bio: A renowned elder of Optina Hermitage who counseled thousands, including Dostoevsky, with humor and spiritual insight.

name: St. Macarius of Optina
title: Venerable
bio: An elder of Optina Hermitage who revived the publication of Patristic texts and guided countless pilgrims.

name: St. Paisius Velichkovsky
title: Venerable
bio: A Ukrainian-born monk who revived hesychast spirituality in Moldavia and translated the Philokalia into Slavonic.

name: St. Demetrios the New of Basarabi
title: Venerable
bio: A Bulgarian shepherd whose relics, discovered incorrupt, became the patron protector of Bucharest.

name: St. Joseph the New of Partoș
title: Bishop
bio: A Metropolitan of Timișoara known for his ascetic life and miracles attributed to his incorrupt relics.

name: St. John Cassian
title: Venerable
bio: A monk who studied under the Desert Fathers and brought Egyptian monastic teaching to the Latin West.

name: St. Martin of Tours
title: Bishop
bio: A former Roman soldier who became bishop of Tours, famed for cutting his cloak in half to clothe a beggar.

name: St. Nicetas the Goth
title: Martyr
bio: A Gothic Christian burned alive for his faith during a persecution among the Goths north of the Danube.

name: St. Sava the Goth
title: Martyr
bio: A Gothic Christian drowned in the Buzău River for his faith, one of the earliest saints venerated in Romania.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — Buzău River, Romania

name: St. Paraskevi of the Balkans (Epivatos)
title: Venerable
bio: A hermitess of Thrace whose relics became especially beloved across Romania, Serbia, and Bulgaria.

name: St. Stefan Milutin, King of Serbia
title: Righteous
bio: A medieval Serbian king renowned for founding numerous monasteries and churches across the Balkans.

name: St. Lazar of Serbia
title: Martyr Prince
bio: Prince of Serbia who fell at the Battle of Kosovo, revered as a martyr for choosing the heavenly kingdom.

name: St. John Vladimir of Serbia
title: Martyr Prince
bio: A pious ruler of Duklja betrayed and beheaded, venerated across the Balkans for his mercy toward his enemies.

name: St. Peter of Korisha
title: Venerable
bio: A Serbian hermit who lived in a cave near Korisha, renowned for his solitude and gift of healing.

name: St. Arsenije I of Serbia
title: Archbishop
bio: Second Archbishop of the Serbian Church who continued St. Sava's work strengthening Serbian Orthodoxy.

name: St. Naum of Ohrid
title: Venerable
bio: A disciple of Cyril and Methodius who continued their missionary work and founded a monastery at Lake Ohrid.

name: St. Clement of Ohrid
title: Bishop
bio: A disciple of Cyril and Methodius who became the first Slavic-speaking bishop, founding a great literary school at Ohrid.

name: St. Gorazd of Moravia
title: Bishop
bio: A disciple and successor of St. Methodius who continued the Slavic liturgical mission in Great Moravia.

name: St. John the Russian
title: Confessor
bio: A Russian soldier enslaved by the Ottomans who kept his faith secretly in Asia Minor, later revered for many miracles.

name: St. George the Confessor of Limnos
title: Confessor
bio: A monk and bishop who suffered imprisonment defending icon veneration during the iconoclast persecutions.

name: St. Stephen the New
title: Venerable Martyr
bio: An Athonite-trained monk martyred in Constantinople for his outspoken defense of holy icons.

name: St. Andrew of Crete
title: Archbishop
bio: Archbishop of Crete and hymnographer, best known for composing the Great Canon of Repentance.

name: Apostle Titus
title: Apostle
bio: A companion of the Apostle Paul who became the first bishop of Crete, guiding its early Christian community.

name: The Ten Martyrs of Crete
title: Martyrs
bio: Ten Christians from various Cretan cities martyred together under Emperor Decius for refusing to sacrifice to idols.

name: St. Nikephoros the Leper
title: Venerable
bio: A 20th-century Cretan man who endured leprosy with patience and became renowned for his gentle holiness.

name: St. Anthimus of Nicomedia
title: Hieromartyr
bio: Bishop of Nicomedia martyred during Diocletian's persecution after refusing to abandon his flock.

name: St. Basiliscus of Comana
title: Martyr
bio: A soldier martyred at Comana, buried near the same place where St. John Chrysostom later reposed.

name: St. Acepsimas of Persia
title: Hieromartyr
bio: A Persian bishop martyred at over one hundred years old during a wave of persecution under Shapur II.

name: St. James the Persian
title: Great Martyr
bio: A Persian courtier who denied Christ under pressure, then repented and endured being cut apart limb by limb for his faith.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — Beth Lapat, Persia

name: St. Anastasius the Persian
title: Venerable Martyr
bio: A former Persian soldier who converted to Christianity, became a monk, and was martyred for destroying idols.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom — near Caesarea, Palestine

name: St. Barbarus the Myrrh-streaming
title: Venerable
bio: A repentant former bandit who lived the rest of his life in prayer and penance, his relics later streaming myrrh.

name: St. David of Euboea
title: Venerable
bio: A hermit of Euboea known for his prophetic gifts, foretelling the recapture of Constantinople.

name: St. Luke of Steiris
title: Venerable
bio: A Byzantine hermit whose monastery in Phocis became one of the great architectural treasures of Greece.

name: St. Christodoulos of Patmos
title: Venerable
bio: Founder of the Monastery of St. John the Theologian on Patmos, obtaining imperial protection for the island's monks.

name: St. Meletios the New
title: Venerable
bio: A Byzantine monk and founder of a monastery on Mount Myoupolis renowned for miracles at his tomb.

name: St. Theoktiste of Lesvos
title: Venerable
bio: A woman who fled to a deserted island near Paros to escape Arab raiders and lived unseen in prayer for decades.

name: St. Anna the New Martyr of Cappadocia
title: New Martyr
bio: A young Cappadocian woman martyred by Ottoman authorities for refusing to abandon her Christian faith.

name: St. Argyra of Constantinople
title: New Martyr
bio: A young married woman imprisoned unjustly and martyred in Constantinople for refusing to convert to Islam.

name: St. George the New of Sofia
title: New Martyr
bio: A young craftsman burned alive in Sofia after refusing to renounce Christianity under Ottoman rule.

name: St. Nicholas the New of Vounaina
title: New Martyr
bio: A young Christian from Epirus stoned to death for defending his faith before Ottoman judges.

name: St. Theodore of Mytilene
title: New Martyr
bio: A young Christian of Lesvos martyred for his faith after being falsely accused before Ottoman authorities.

name: St. Moses the Black
title: Venerable
bio: A former robber chieftain in Egypt who repented and became a monk in the Skete desert, renowned for his humility and later ordained a priest before being martyred by raiders.

name: St. Photini, the Samaritan Woman
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: The Samaritan woman who met Christ at Jacob's Well, was converted, and became a fervent evangelist, later martyred in Rome under Nero.

name: St. Romanos the Melodist
title: Hymnographer
bio: A deacon of Syrian birth who became the greatest hymnographer of the Byzantine Church, composing the Kontakion of the Nativity and hundreds of other hymns.

name: St. Kassiani the Hymnographer
title: Hymnographer
bio: A learned Byzantine abbess and poet, famed for composing the Hymn of Kassiani sung during Holy Week, one of the few works by a woman in the Orthodox liturgical tradition.

name: St. Theodora of Arta
title: Venerable
bio: Empress of Epirus who, after enduring slander and exile, was reconciled with her husband and later became a nun, known for her charity and patience in suffering.

name: St. Gregory of Tours
title: Bishop
bio: Bishop and historian of Gaul whose writings, including the History of the Franks, preserved the memory of early Western saints venerated before the Great Schism.

name: St. Nino, Equal-to-the-Apostles
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: A woman of Cappadocian origin who preached the Gospel in Georgia and, through miracles and her cross of grapevines, brought the Georgian royal court to Christianity.

name: Sts. Barlaam and Josaphat
title: Ascetics
bio: A monk and the Indian prince he converted to Christianity, whose legendary story of renunciation and asceticism became one of the most popular tales of the medieval Christian world.

name: St. Juliana of Nicomedia
title: Great Martyr
bio: A young Christian woman tortured and beheaded at Nicomedia after refusing to marry a pagan official and to renounce her faith.

name: St. Theodosia of Constantinople
title: Martyr
bio: A nun martyred in Constantinople for defending the holy icon of Christ over the Chalke Gate during the Iconoclast persecution.

name: St. Symeon the Stylite
title: Venerable
bio: A Syrian ascetic who spent decades living atop a pillar in prayer and fasting, becoming a renowned spiritual guide visited by pilgrims from across the ancient world.

name: St. Daniel of Moscow
title: Prince
bio: The first Prince of Moscow, celebrated for his peaceful rule, humility, and the monastery he founded, later becoming the patron saint of the city.

name: St. Philaret the Merciful
title: Righteous
bio: A wealthy landowner of Asia Minor who gave away his fortune to the poor, trusting in Providence, and whose granddaughter became empress of Byzantium.

name: Sts. Joachim and Anna
title: Ancestors of God
bio: The righteous parents of the Theotokos, who, after years of childlessness, received the Virgin Mary as a gift from God in their old age.

name: St. Zosimas of Solovki
title: Venerable
bio: Co-founder of the Solovetsky Monastery in the White Sea, whose ascetic labors established one of Russia's great centers of monasticism.

name: St. Savvatii of Solovki
title: Venerable
bio: A monk who, seeking solitude, settled on the remote Solovetsky Islands and co-founded the monastery that became a beacon of Russian monasticism.

name: St. Nil Sorsky
title: Venerable
bio: A Russian monastic reformer who, after studying hesychasm on Mount Athos, promoted a life of poverty and inner prayer among Russian monks.

name: St. Tikhon of Zadonsk
title: Bishop
bio: A Russian bishop who retired to Zadonsk Monastery, where he wrote spiritual works and became known for his humility and care for the poor.

name: St. John the Almsgiver
title: Patriarch of Alexandria
bio: Patriarch of Alexandria renowned for his extraordinary generosity to the poor, distributing the wealth of his see to the needy and refugees of his time.

name: St. Gregory the Illuminator
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: Apostle to Armenia who converted King Tiridates III and the Armenian nation to Christianity, becoming the first Catholicos of the Armenian Church.

name: Apostle and Evangelist John the Theologian
title: Apostle, Evangelist and Theologian
bio: Beloved disciple of Christ, author of the Fourth Gospel, three Epistles and the Book of Revelation, who reposed peacefully in old age at Ephesus.

name: Apostle James, Son of Alphaeus
title: Apostle
bio: One of the Twelve Apostles who preached the Gospel in Judea and Egypt, where he was crucified for his faith.

name: Apostle Simon the Zealot
title: Apostle
bio: One of the Twelve Apostles, formerly a Zealot, who preached in Egypt, Africa and the Caucasus before being martyred in Abkhazia.

name: Apostle Matthias
title: Apostle
bio: Chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot among the Twelve, he preached in Judea and Cappadocia before his martyrdom in Jerusalem.

name: Apostle Barnabas
title: Apostle of the Seventy
bio: A Cypriot Levite and close companion of the Apostle Paul on his early missionary journeys, and the first bishop of Cyprus, martyred at Salamis.

name: St. Nicholas of Japan
title: Equal-to-the-Apostles, Enlightener of Japan
bio: Russian missionary bishop who founded the Orthodox Church in Japan, translating the Scriptures and services into Japanese over half a century of ministry.

name: St. John of Shanghai and San Francisco
title: Wonderworker of Shanghai and San Francisco
bio: Ascetic bishop of the Russian diaspora renowned for his humility and miracles, who cared for orphans in Shanghai and led the Church in Western Europe and San Francisco.

name: St. Sophrony of Essex
title: Elder of Essex
bio: Disciple of St. Silouan the Athonite who brought hesychast monastic tradition to Western Europe, founding the Monastery of St. John the Baptist in Essex, England.

name: St. Maria of Paris
title: New Martyr of Paris
bio: Russian émigré nun who sheltered Jews and resistance members in Nazi-occupied Paris, dying in the Ravensbrück concentration camp.

name: St. Justin (Popović) of Ćelije
title: New Chrysostom of Serbia
bio: Serbian theologian and monk celebrated for his writings on Orthodox dogmatics, who spent his final decades confined to Ćelije Monastery.

name: St. Gabriel (Urgebadze) of Georgia
title: Fool-for-Christ of Georgia
bio: Beloved Georgian elder and fool-for-Christ, famed for his boldness of faith under Soviet rule and his ministry at Samtavro Convent.

name: St. Genevieve of Paris
title: Patroness of Paris
bio: Fifth-century ascetic credited with saving Paris from Attila the Hun through prayer, venerated ever since as the city's patroness.

name: St. Alban of Britain
title: Protomartyr of Britain
bio: The first recorded Christian martyr of Britain, executed for sheltering a persecuted priest and taking his place at the executioner's block.

name: St. Augustine of Canterbury
title: Apostle to the English, first Archbishop of Canterbury
bio: Roman monk sent by Pope Gregory the Dialogist to evangelize the Anglo-Saxons, becoming the first Archbishop of Canterbury.

name: St. Gregory the Dialogist
title: Pope of Rome
bio: Pope of Rome and prolific author of the 'Dialogues,' who reformed the liturgy and sent missionaries to evangelize England.

name: St. Brigid of Kildare
title: Abbess of Kildare
bio: One of Ireland's most beloved saints, founder of the monastery at Kildare and renowned for her charity toward the poor.

name: St. Columba of Iona
title: Apostle to the Picts, Abbot of Iona
bio: Irish monk who founded the monastery of Iona, from which he evangelized the Picts of Scotland.

name: St. Cuthbert of Lindisfarne
title: Bishop of Lindisfarne
bio: Beloved bishop and hermit of Northumbria, celebrated for his miracles and his love of solitude on the Farne Islands.

name: St. David of Wales
title: Patron of Wales, Archbishop of Menevia
bio: Ascetic monk-bishop and founder of monasteries across Wales, revered ever since as the nation's patron saint.

name: St. Kevin of Glendalough
title: Abbot of Glendalough
bio: Irish hermit whose life of prayer amid the wilderness of Glendalough attracted disciples and gave rise to a great monastic settlement.
